metadata.title: Momentum Contrast for Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
metadata.authors: Kaiming He, Haoqi Fan, Yuxin Wu, Saining Xie, Ross Girshick

nodes.name: Unsupervised Visual Representation Learning
nodes.statement: Learn visual feature representations from unlabeled images such that the resulting features transfer well to downstream vision tasks (detection, segmentation, classification) via fine-tuning.
nodes.statement_clean: Train an image encoder without labels so its features transfer to downstream vision tasks.

nodes.name: Dynamic Dictionary Look-up for Contrastive Learning
nodes.statement: Train an encoder $f_q$ such that an encoded query $q = f_q(x_q)$ matches its positive key $k_+$ and is dissimilar to all other (negative) keys in a dictionary $\{k_0, k_1, k_2, \dots\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Build an encoder whose query is similar to one matching key and dissimilar to many negative keys in a dictionary.
assumptions: Encoded query $q$ and a set of encoded keys $\{k_0, k_1, \dots\}$ exist
There is a single positive key $k_+$ that $q$ matches
conclusions: A contrastive loss $L_q$ is low when $q$ is similar to $k_+$ and dissimilar to other keys

nodes.name: Contrastive Loss
nodes.statement: A loss function that measures similarities of sample pairs in a representation space. Its target can vary on-the-fly during training and is defined in terms of the data representation computed by a network.

nodes.name: InfoNCE Loss
nodes.statement: $L_q = -\log \frac{\exp(q \cdot k_+/\tau)}{\sum_{i=0}^{K} \exp(q \cdot k_i / \tau)}$, where $\tau$ is a temperature hyper-parameter and the sum is over one positive and $K$ negative samples.
nodes.statement_clean: A $(K{+}1)$-way softmax cross-entropy loss that classifies the query $q$ as its positive key $k_+$ among $K$ negatives.

nodes.name: Query Encoder $f_q$ and Key Encoder $f_k$
nodes.statement: Encoder networks producing the query representation $q = f_q(x_q)$ and key representation $k = f_k(x_k)$ from input samples $x_q, x_k$.

nodes.name: Dictionary as a Queue
nodes.statement: Maintain the dictionary of keys as a FIFO queue: the current mini-batch is enqueued, and the oldest mini-batch is dequeued. The queue size $K$ is decoupled from the mini-batch size and is a hyper-parameter.

nodes.name: Momentum Update of Key Encoder
nodes.statement: Update key-encoder parameters by $\theta_k \leftarrow m \theta_k + (1-m)\theta_q$, where $m \in [0,1)$ is the momentum coefficient. Only $\theta_q$ is updated by back-propagation.
nodes.statement_clean: The key encoder is an exponential moving average of the query encoder; no gradients flow through it.

nodes.name: Instance Discrimination Pretext Task
nodes.statement: Treat a query and a key as a positive pair if they originate from the same image (two random augmentations / views of it), and as negatives otherwise.

nodes.name: Shuffling BN
nodes.statement: When training the key encoder $f_k$ across multiple GPUs, shuffle the sample order of the current mini-batch before distributing it among GPUs (and shuffle back after encoding); the order for $f_q$ is unchanged. Ensures BN statistics for $q$ and its positive key come from different sub-batches.

nodes.name: InfoNCE Contrastive Loss
nodes.statement: $L_q = -\log \dfrac{\exp(q\cdot k_+/\tau)}{\sum_{i=0}^{K} \exp(q\cdot k_i/\tau)}$ \quad (Eq. 1).

nodes.name: Momentum Update Rule
nodes.statement: $\theta_k \leftarrow m\,\theta_k + (1-m)\,\theta_q$ \quad (Eq. 2).

nodes.name: Momentum Contrast (MoCo)
nodes.statement: PyTorch-style mini-batch training procedure that maintains a queue of encoded keys and updates the key encoder as a momentum moving average of the query encoder, optimizing the InfoNCE loss.
nodes.statement_clean: MoCo training: encode query/key from two augmentations, compute InfoNCE against the queue, SGD on $f_q$, momentum-update $f_k$, then enqueue new keys and dequeue old.
nodes.pseudocode: for x in loader: x_q = aug(x); x_k = aug(x); q = f_q(x_q); k = f_k(x_k).detach(); l_pos = bmm(q, k); l_neg = mm(q, queue); logits = cat([l_pos, l_neg]); labels = 0; loss = CE(logits/t, labels); loss.backward(); update(f_q); f_k.params = m*f_k.params + (1-m)*f_q.params; enqueue(queue, k); dequeue(queue).

nodes.name: End-to-End Contrastive Mechanism
nodes.statement: Use samples in the current mini-batch as the dictionary; both query and key encoders are updated by back-propagation. Dictionary size is coupled with the mini-batch size.
nodes.origin_citation: Hadsell-Chopra-LeCun 2006 / van den Oord 2018 / Hjelm 2019 etc.

nodes.name: Memory Bank
nodes.statement: Maintain a bank of representations of all dataset samples; for each mini-batch sample dictionary keys randomly from the bank with no back-propagation. Bank entries are updated when the corresponding sample is last seen.

nodes.name: ImageNet-1M Linear Classification
nodes.statement: Pre-train MoCo unsupervisedly on ImageNet-1M, freeze features, train a linear classifier, evaluate top-1 accuracy. With ResNet-50 and $K=65536$, $m=0.999$, MoCo reaches 60.6%; with R50w4x reaches 68.6%.

nodes.name: Ablation: Contrastive Loss Mechanisms vs. K
nodes.statement: Compare end-to-end, memory-bank, and MoCo on IN-1M linear classification while sweeping $K \in \{256, \dots, 65536\}$. MoCo benefits monotonically from larger $K$ (54.7 to 60.6) and is best of the three, especially at large $K$.

nodes.name: Ablation: Momentum Coefficient $m$
nodes.statement: On IN-1M with $K=4096$: $m=0$ fails; $m=0.9 \to 55.2$; $m=0.99 \to 57.8$; $m=0.999 \to 59.0$; $m=0.9999 \to 58.9$. A slowly progressing key encoder (large $m$) is essential.

nodes.name: PASCAL VOC Object Detection
nodes.statement: Fine-tune Faster R-CNN (R50-C4 / R50-dilated-C5) initialized from MoCo IN-1M or IG-1B on VOC trainval07+12, evaluate on test2007. MoCo IG-1B exceeds ImageNet-supervised pre-training by up to +0.9 AP50, +3.7 AP, +4.9 AP75.

nodes.name: COCO Detection and Instance Segmentation
nodes.statement: Fine-tune Mask R-CNN (R50-FPN / R50-C4) on COCO train2017, evaluate on val2017. With 2x schedule, MoCo beats ImageNet-supervised pre-training in all metrics on both backbones.

nodes.name: More Downstream Tasks (Keypoint, DensePose, LVIS, Cityscapes, VOC-seg)
nodes.statement: Across COCO keypoint detection, COCO dense pose, LVIS instance segmentation, Cityscapes instance and semantic segmentation, and VOC semantic segmentation, MoCo IG-1B is on par or better than the ImageNet-supervised counterpart in 7 of these tasks.

nodes.name: Shuffling BN Ablation
nodes.statement: Without shuffling BN, MoCo overfits the pretext task: pretext training accuracy reaches >99.9% while kNN ImageNet validation accuracy collapses, indicating BN-leak "cheating".

nodes.name: iNaturalist Fine-Grained Classification
nodes.statement: Fine-tune R50 end-to-end on iNaturalist 2018 (~437k images, 8142 classes). MoCo IN-1M = 65.6%, MoCo IG-1B = 65.8%, supervised IN-1M = 66.1%, random init = 61.8%.

nodes.name: Two Desiderata: Large and Consistent Dictionaries
nodes.statement: Hypothesis motivating MoCo: good contrastive features require dictionaries that are (i) large (so as to densely sample the high-dimensional visual space) and (ii) consistent (keys produced by similar encoders), but existing mechanisms achieve only one of the two.

nodes.name: Why Naive Copy of $f_q$ to $f_k$ Fails
nodes.statement: Copying $f_k \leftarrow f_q$ at every step (ignoring queue gradients) yields poor results: the rapidly changing key encoder destroys consistency among the keys stored in the queue. The momentum update fixes this.

nodes.name: Memory Bank's Inconsistency
nodes.statement: In a memory bank, sampled keys correspond to encoder snapshots scattered over the past epoch, hence are inconsistent. MoCo avoids this by encoding fresh keys with a slow-moving encoder, producing consistent keys at the cost of only the most recent mini-batches.

nodes.name: Normalization and Schedules for Transfer
nodes.statement: Two practical issues for transferring MoCo features: (i) feature distributions differ from supervised pre-training, motivating tuned BN during fine-tuning; (ii) controlled fine-tuning schedules (e.g., 1x/2x) are used so MoCo and supervised baselines are compared fairly.

nodes.name: Better Pretext Tasks for MoCo
nodes.statement: MoCo's gain from IN-1M to IG-1B is positive but small, suggesting larger-scale data is not fully exploited. Whether more advanced pretext tasks (e.g., masked auto-encoding analogous to BERT) can unlock further gains is open.

nodes.name: Large Mini-Batch Optimization for End-to-End Contrastive
nodes.statement: End-to-end contrastive training is bottlenecked by the open problem of optimizing very large mini-batches; even with linear learning-rate scaling, accuracy drops at 1024-batch and it is unclear if the trend extrapolates to larger $K$.

nodes.name: Initialize key encoder from query encoder
nodes.statement: $f_k.\text{params} \leftarrow f_q.\text{params}$.

nodes.name: Mini-batch loop
nodes.statement: For each mini-batch $x$ of $N$ samples loaded from the dataset, perform steps 3-9 below.

nodes.name: Augment two views
nodes.statement: $x_q = \mathrm{aug}(x);\; x_k = \mathrm{aug}(x)$ — two random augmentations of the same images form positive pairs.

nodes.name: Encode queries and keys
nodes.statement: $q = f_q.\mathrm{forward}(x_q)$ (size $N\times C$); $k = f_k.\mathrm{forward}(x_k)$, then $k = k.\mathrm{detach}()$ (no gradient to keys).

nodes.name: Form positive and negative logits
nodes.statement: $l_{\text{pos}} = \mathrm{bmm}(q, k)$ ($N\times 1$); $l_{\text{neg}} = \mathrm{mm}(q, \text{queue})$ ($N\times K$); $\text{logits} = \mathrm{cat}([l_{\text{pos}}, l_{\text{neg}}], \text{dim}=1)$.

nodes.name: Compute InfoNCE loss
nodes.statement: $\text{labels} = \mathbf{0}$ (positives are at index 0); $\text{loss} = \mathrm{CrossEntropyLoss}(\text{logits}/\tau, \text{labels})$ — implements Eq. (1).

nodes.name: SGD update of query encoder
nodes.statement: $\text{loss.backward}();\; \text{update}(f_q.\text{params})$ — only $\theta_q$ receives gradients.

nodes.name: Momentum update of key encoder
nodes.statement: $f_k.\text{params} \leftarrow m \cdot f_k.\text{params} + (1-m) \cdot f_q.\text{params}$ — implements Eq. (2).

nodes.name: Enqueue current keys, dequeue oldest
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{enqueue}(\text{queue}, k);\; \mathrm{dequeue}(\text{queue})$ — keep dictionary size at $K$, replacing the oldest mini-batch.
